title: POC Scenario: Pricing-Latency Tradeoffs Canvas
content:
Purpose and scope:
This canvas is a lightweight, pragmatic decision tool for solutions engineers running customer POCs where latency requirements and cost/pricing constraints pull in opposite directions. It is intended to be used during pre-onboarding and the first two sprints of a POC to: 1) align the customer on tradeoffs, 2) choose an initial serving configuration (hosted / dedicated / private variant), and 3) define experiments and acceptance criteria that drive the rollout.

How to use this doc (quick):
- Run a 30–45 minute alignment workshop with the customer + product/infra owner. Use the scenario matrix below to pick a primary scenario (A/B/C) and a fallback.
- Translate chosen scenario into a config stub (model family, precision, batching, cache policy, infra target).
- Implement two short experiments (latency-first and cost-first) and measure the three core metrics (p95 latency, tokens-per-USD, functional accuracy on sample prompts).
- Use the escalation triggers and decision rules to pick final deployment mode after 2 weeks of data.

Definitions (for this canvas):
- Latency-first: target p95 < 250ms for 0–512 tokens (interactive UI).
- Cost-first: target tokens-per-USD >= baseline customer target (TBD per account).
- Mixed: acceptable p95 <= 600ms and tokens-per-USD within 10% of cost-first.

Scenario matrix (pick one primary + one fallback):
- Scenario A — Latency-first (interactive support / chat):
  - Typical workload: many short chats, 60–90 TPS bursts, strict UX SLOs.
  - Initial config suggestion: small-ish decoder model family with low-latency kernels, FP16 or int8 quantized variant if QA passes; continuous batching disabled or very tight max batch sizes; aggressive prefix cache for system prompts.
  - Infra: Dedicated pool (pinned GPUs) or hosted with latency SLA; region co-located with UI.
  - Acceptance criteria (after 7 days): p95 <= 250ms for 0–512 tokens, error rate < 1%, functional accuracy loss < 2% vs baseline.
  - Cost expectation: higher $/token, document for customer tradeoff.

- Scenario B — Cost-first (background processing / async generation):
  - Typical workload: large batched document summaries, embeddings, offline pipelines.
  - Initial config suggestion: larger model family with batching enabled, quantized int8 where possible; longer queue depth, autoscaling with spot/backfill friendly nodes.
  - Infra: Hosted standard or Dedicated with autoscale; can use lower-cost regions.
  - Acceptance criteria (after 7 days): tokens-per-USD >= target, throughput meets batch SLA (jobs/hour), p95 acceptable per async SLA.

- Scenario C — Mixed (constrained budget, soft latency):
  - Typical workload: mix of interactive and async, occasional bursts.
  - Initial config suggestion: two-tier routing policy (hosted low-latency pool for short requests, cost-optimized pool for long/async requests), prefix cache + KV warm-up, dynamic model fallback policy (fp16 -> quantized variant).
  - Infra: Hybrid (Hosted + Dedicated or Private routing).
  - Acceptance criteria: p95 <= 600ms for interactive subset, tokens-per-USD within 10% of cost-first.

Decision heuristics (short):
- If strict UX requirement or legal/regulatory requirement to isolate data -> prefer Dedicated or Private.
- If budget constraint dominates and workloads are batchy -> prefer Cost-first with autoscaling and larger batches.
- If customer expects spiky interactive load but limited budget -> choose Mixed and run routing experiments.

Experiment plan (two parallel experiments, week 0–2):
- Experiment 1: Latency-optimised path
  - Model: candidate A (smaller family) FP16
  - Serving config: 1 GPU per node, low batching (max batch 8), KV/prefix caching enabled, warmup script run at deploy.
  - Metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, tokens-per-USD.
  - Run length: 7 full days of representative traffic.

- Experiment 2: Cost-optimised path
  - Model: candidate B (larger family) int8 quantized
  - Serving config: batching enabled (max batch 128), higher concurrency per GPU, autoscale policy with 2 min cool-down.
  - Metrics: throughput (tokens/s), avg cost-per-request, functional accuracy on evaluation prompts.
  - Run length: 7 full days of representative traffic.

Composable acceptance checks (scriptable):
- CHECK_1: p95_latency <= threshold -> PASS/FAIL
- CHECK_2: tokens_per_usd >= threshold -> PASS/FAIL
- CHECK_3: eval_accuracy_drop <= 3% -> PASS/FAIL
- If both experiments pass different checks, present tradeoff table to customer and use weighted scoring (customer weights captured in workshop).

Roles and quick RACI: (use short contacts during POC)
- Solutions lead (owner): Aisha Patel - coordinates experiments, leads customer workshop.
- SRE / infra contact: Marco Liu - deploys pools, validates autoscale rules, monitors infra costs.
- Applied ML / model QA: Jenna Morales - validates quantization accuracy and kernel compatibility.
- Customer PM: (customer name here) - signs off on acceptance weights and provides sample prompt set.

Timeline (compact):
- Day -3 to 0: workshop + scenario selection; provision infra stubs, confirm prompts and metrics; deploy initial config.
- Day 1–7: run Experiments 1 & 2 in parallel; daily checks, quick standups; warm caches with synthetic runs as needed.
- Day 8–10: analyze, present tradeoffs, pick final path (Latency/Cost/Mixed).
- Day 11–14: implement final rollout config, do canary, cutover, and handoff to customer success.

Contingency triggers & playbook snippets:
- Trigger: p95 > SLA for two consecutive days -> action: scale out dedicated pool by +1 node, temporarily route traffic to fallback model, open SE-incident channel.
- Trigger: tokens-per-USD > budget threshold -> action: switch to higher batch window + enable quantized fallback, pause non-essential background jobs.
- Trigger: quantized variant causes >5% eval accuracy regression -> action: immediate rollback to FP16, tag quantization PR for additional QA, notify customer and schedule remediation.

Operational checklist for first deploy (copyable):
- [ ] Confirm sample prompt set uploaded to shared bucket + labeled expected outputs.
- [ ] Bake warmup script and confirm KV cache priming run.
- [ ] Attach tracing and per-route dashboard in Redwood Console; ensure token-level cost is visible.
- [ ] Configure rollout policy: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on error/latency thresholds.
- [ ] Create cost alert: projected 7-day burn > X% of customer budget.
- [ ] Create SLO alerts (p95 latency, error rate) with escalation to oncall.

Deliverables at handoff (what we give customer at the end of POC):
- Short report: experiment results + decision table (latency vs cost vs accuracy).
- Deployment manifest: final model version + infra config + rollout policy.
- Runbook: post-cutover monitoring + cost controls + rollback steps.
- Optional: playbook for moving from Hosted to Dedicated or Private including security checklist and KMS integration notes.

Communication snippets (Slack/email) to speed approvals:
- To product/security: "Quick FYI: POC will run two serving configs in parallel this week. We will route interactive traffic to a low-latency pool and batch jobs to a cost pool. We'll notify if infra changes required > 2 nodes."
- To customer PM: "We proposed two experiments (latency-first and cost-first). After 7 days we will show a tradeoff table and recommend the final deployment mode. Please confirm priority weights for latency vs cost."

Notes / open questions to capture in workshop:
- Customer weight for latency vs cost (numeric 0–10).
- Regulatory data residency or isolation requirements.
- Will the prompt distribution during the POC be representative of production? If not, plan a synthetic trace.
- Acceptance threshold for functional accuracy (by feature).

Appendix: quick template for scoring table (use spreadsheet):
- Columns: scenario, p95_latency_score (0-10), cost_score (0-10), accuracy_score (0-10), weighted_total -> final_rank.

End note: this canvas is intentionally lightweight — copy into a customer-specific sheet and record the chosen numeric weights and final experiment outputs. Keep the runbook and final manifest in the project folder so the customer success team can onboard the Dedicated/Private migration if chosen.
